title: Generalised André-Pink-Zannier conjecture for Shimura varieties of Abelian type
reviewed_version: Publisher version of record, DOI10.1007/s10240-025-00154-4, IHES141(2025)249–331, 83 physical PDF pages; distinct arXiv2111.11216v4 source retained without equivalence assertion.
summary: Core norm-comparison invocation fails its explicit connected-stabilizer hypothesis. Independent acceptance supplies the needed finite-component repair for the actual fixed centralizer, with unchanged uniform weight constant and no additive constant. Four auxiliary defects remain Minor; the main theorem is not refuted.

correction.statement: After excluding finitely many bad primes and divisors of the fixed component-group order, first form Y=G/F0, then X=Y/(F/F0). Averaging proves invariant base change; finite generation, torsion-free flatness and smooth geometric quotient fibers give smooth X and G->X. The normalization argument, with genuine coactions, gives integral X->orbit closure and the same integral-point criterion. Section6.3 then has identical convex zero sets and unchanged weight constants, with no additive constant.
correction.retained_dependencies: Connected reductive quotient results in Section7.3, standard finite etale free quotient facts, normalization/smooth base-change interfaces; no full new proof of every external foundation.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: Theorem6.1/Section6.1 footnote12 requires connected reductive stabilizer fibers. For SO4?SO5 on W4?1, the full centralizer is {diag(?I4,1)}=mu2 at every odd prime. Bounded-index subgroups at large primes contain Omega4+, whose tensor-product representation has the same two scalar commutant blocks; the rational and residual Tate conditions and trivial abelianization hold. Faithful adjoint representation keeps the nonidentity action on W. Thus the abstract operative conditions do not imply the missing connectedness. No actual Shimura Galois realization is claimed.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: At all sufficiently large primes for the fixed F over Q, spread out to smooth F, connected reductive F0 and finite-etale Q=F/F0 of invertible order. Let Y=G/F0 and X=Spec(R[G]^F)=Y/Q. Averaging gives invariant base change; finite-group invariant theory gives finite generation, and torsion-free DVR flatness plus free geometric quotient fibers gives smooth X and smooth surjective G->X. Normalization is equivariant under a genuine coaction, and Lemma7.10's normality, quasi-finiteness and one-special-orbit proof uses only the repaired quotient facts, connected G and stabilizer dimensions. It gives integral X->orbit closure. Propositions7.14?7.15 yield the same barred integral-point criterion, so Section6.3 has identical convex zero sets and unchanged weight set C(Sigma(rho)), without additive constant. Section5.1.3 permits the finite excluded primes.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: This full repair proves that the missing interface can be restored in the actual application. It does not validate the authors' literal invocation; the inequality and final theorem are not refuted.
independent_acceptance.severity_rationale: Review-contract0.7.1 distinguishes a demonstrated invalid core derivation from repair length and theorem survival. Retain Major for the original invocation, while marking the repair verified. Native recommendation to lower to Minor is recorded without falsely claiming consensus.

check.all_hypotheses: Open localgroups,ZarGL2; forq>max(p0,D,3), boundedindex residualgroup containsSL2Fq, so absoluteirreducibility/scalarcentralizers hold.

impact.severity_basis: Strict-index assertion proved and actual eventual-prime uses survive.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: At one prime p0 use the inverse image of upper unipotent C_p0 in GL2(Z_p0), full groups at other primes, and replace that factor by the principal congruence kernel. Index is p0 and dagger residual subgroup changes from C to1. problems.title: Lemma5.12 kernel-intersection subgroup need not satisfy stronger centralizer equality
assumptions: M=SL2overF17,e=2 dividesappropriate center order; U finitecompactresidualsubgroup.

check.independent_calculation: whw^-1=-h; adw centralizesprojectiveh butno centrallymodifiedliftcentralizesh. FiniteSL2F17order4896; centralizerh16; inverseimageprojectivecentralizer32.

counterevidence: Commutatorproof establishesweaker Z_Mad(adU) subset imageZ_M(U[e]); actualLemma5.11needs onlythisandTatecentralizer.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: In SL2(F17), g=diag(2,9) has order8 and U[2]=<diag(4,13)> has order4. The Weyl element w conjugates h to ?h, so its adjoint class centralizes ad(U[2]) although no central modification centralizes h. This refutes the specified construction, not existence of some bounded-index U'.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: The commutator map of a lift centralizing ad(U) is a homomorphism U->Z(M); the kernel intersection U[e] kills it. Hence Z_Mad(ad U) is contained in the image of Z_M(U[e]). The actual bounded-index Tate use identifies the latter with the center, which is enough for Lemma5.11. General stronger existential equality remains unverified, not asserted false. Historical finite-field diagnostics were not rerun.

problems.title: Integral-point stability need not define a group-scheme action
assumptions: Gclosed smoothreductive; A finitelygenerated. Normality andgenericfiberequalitynotrequired.

impact.severity_basis: The two actual applications satisfy genuine coaction stability; this repair also supports the newly verified finite-component normalization argument.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: The actual source has unbarred integral-point stability. A=Z_p[pt,t^p?t]?Z_p[t,t^-1] is stable under all u in Z_p^? because (u^p?u)/p is integral, but t is absent (its reduction cannot have degree1 in F_p[t^p?t]). Coaction delta(t^p?t)=(t^p?t)s^p+t(s^p?s) has coefficient?t, so it does not land in A[s,s^-1].
independent_acceptance.repair_check: Require genuine group-scheme coaction. For invariant quotient algebras commuting left/right translations and flat base change give it; for normalization, smooth base change preserves normality and the dominant action uniquely lifts, with action law by uniqueness. Both actual applications and the new P1 normalization meet this stronger condition.

problems.title: Frobenius-twisted semisimple embeddings give infinitely many geometric conjugacy classes

independent_acceptance.reasoning: For fixed p>5 and n4, graph subgroups S_r={diag(g,Frob^r(g))} are closed connected semisimple. Their Lie algebras have common fixed second block and image first block, forcing a conjugator to be block diagonal. Applying a unipotent gives nonzero polynomial terms of degrees p^r and p^s; equality forces r=s, even over algebraic closure.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: S_r(F_p) is always diagonal SL2(F_p), so this is not a counterexample to the required Nori-envelope setting. The actual center and outer-group bounds follow from finitely many root data/isogeny types of rank<=n; embedding finiteness is unnecessary. No counterexample to LemmaB.5 or TheoremB.1 asserted.
